svg.text: For kitchen equipment, exhaust, gas, plumbing and electrical vendors · plan at 1:25 and elevation at 1:40 on A3
Hot line elevation · back wall seen from inside · 1:40 on A3
gas manifold at 0.40 m · dot = appliance valve
water point: hot + cold (C = cold only)
drain line to the grease trap
power point, see the services list
make-up (fresh) air grille in the ceiling
Duct along the wall, round the corner
LPG line, copper, from the cage
Solenoid valve on the gas entry
by the rear exit · on backup
Allow about 4,000–5,000 m³/h for the whole hood (vendor to
size); about 8 m/s in the 0.40 × 0.40 duct. ESP + carbon filter
before the fan. No roof stack: apartment above, parking behind.
Make-up air about 80% of the exhaust, interlocked.
4 × 19 kg LPG in a locked, ventilated cage on the right strip.
A valve per appliance; solenoid shuts off with the fan or the
hood suppression; leak detector at the line entry.
All kitchen drains to the grease trap, then the grey-water line
(never the biodigester). Epoxy floor falls to the channel drain.
Shop supply: three-phase, about 15–20 kW. Backup 7.5 kVA
covers the fridges, rails, fan, ESP, lights. Not the ACs.
